title: Rentomojo debuts at 19% premium, then rallies further on NSE
excerpt: The furniture-rental platform opened at ₹482.45, a 19.42% premium to its ₹404 IPO price, and climbed to ₹526.70 within an hour; the ₹1,255.57-crore issue was subscribed nearly 73 times.
body:
• Rentomojo opened at ₹482.45 on the NSE on Thursday — a 19.42% premium over its ₹404 IPO price — and rallied about 9% more to ₹526.70 within the first hour, a ~30% debut-day gain.
  • The ₹1,255.57 crore IPO was subscribed nearly 73 times, with institutional demand leading at over 177 times.
  • FY26 revenue was ₹387 crore (up 45.5%) and profit ₹104 crore (up 142%), but analysts flag a rich valuation of about 41x FY26 earnings.
  • The fresh issue is only ₹150 crore of the total — the rest was an offer for sale by existing investors, including Accel.

MUMBAI — Rentomojo, India's first listed furniture-rental platform, made a strong debut on Thursday, opening nearly 20% above its IPO price and extending the rally within the first hour of trade.

The stock opened at ₹482.45 on the NSE, a 19.42% premium over the ₹404 issue price, and rose about 9% further to ₹526.70 in less than an hour, taking debut-day gains to roughly 30%. On the BSE it opened at ₹480, up 18.81%. The early rally added more than ₹460 crore to the company's market capitalization, taking it to nearly ₹5,484 crore, according to The Economic Times.

Why the IPO drew such heat

The ₹1,255.57-crore IPO, which ran from September 9 to 11, was subscribed nearly 73 times its offer size, according to NSE data cited by Mint — 158.68 crore shares bid against 2.17 crore on offer. Qualified institutional buyers led demand at 177.29 times, non-institutional investors came in at 67.93 times, and the retail portion was subscribed 15.59 times.

A day before the IPO opened, the company raised ₹376 crore from 41 anchor investors. The issue comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 crore and an offer for sale of 2.73 crore shares worth about ₹1,106 crore by existing shareholders, including Accel — which held a 20.9% stake — Edelweiss Discovery Fund, IDG Ventures, and founder and CEO Geetansh Bamania.

Grey-market signals pointed the way: trackers showed the stock trading at a premium of about ₹134 over the issue price on September 9, implying a listing around ₹538. The actual debut landed below that mark.

The business behind the listing

Founded in 2012 and headquartered in Bengaluru, Rentomojo runs a full-stack subscription platform renting furniture, appliances, and household durables — beds, sofas, washing machines, refrigerators, TVs, and water purifiers — with delivery, installation, maintenance, and relocation bundled in. It has no listed peers in India, which means the market is effectively setting the segment's benchmark valuation.

The operating numbers are strong. Revenue from operations rose 45.5% to ₹387 crore in FY26, while profit jumped 142% to ₹104 crore. The company had 253,825 live subscribers across 29 cities as of March 31, 2026, about 851,000 live items on its books, 20 warehouses, 82 experience stores, and an inventory occupancy rate above 83%. Private-label manufacturing with Dixon Technologies has added a new line to the business.

“Rentomojo's 19% listing pop has already priced in much of the near-term optimism, and at around 41x FY26 P/E, the valuation cushion remains thin.”

— Shivani Nyati, Head of Wealth, Swastika Investmart

Can the debut-day mojo last?

Analysts are split between the growth story and the price being asked for it. Sunny Agrawal of SBI Securities argued investors should hold from a medium- to long-term perspective, calling Rentomojo “a play on urban mobility” with a recurring subscription model and growing subscriber base, and noting “fabulous growth during the last two years.”

But Nyati of Swastika Investmart cautioned that the listing pop has already priced in much of the near-term optimism, and until profitability and asset-utilization metrics show sustained improvement, the stock is better suited to a wait-and-watch approach — suggesting a stop loss at ₹430, below the listing price.

The use of proceeds tells its own story: of the ₹150 crore fresh issue, ₹70 crore goes toward repaying borrowings and ₹42.5 crore toward lease and licence fees for warehouses and experience stores, with the rest for general corporate purposes. Total outstanding borrowings stood at ₹258.3 crore as of June 30, 2026. Debt reduction is a structural positive — but the fundamentals will have to keep compounding to justify the price the market has put on the debut.
image_caption: Coverage of Rentomojo's market debut. The furniture-rental platform opened at Rs 482.45 on the NSE — a 19.42% premium over its Rs 404 IPO price — and rallied about 9% further within the first hour of trade.
nri_angle: Rentomojo's debut sets the benchmark valuation for India's rental-economy sector and signals to global investors how the Indian consumer subscription market is being priced.
